new_codes.title: Power demand: efficiency increment sits on the net-exports row
new_codes.where: Mitigation row 3719 (D3719 = D3742 'Net Exports (Imports negative)', F:J net-export data egy.mit.nxp.ecy; L3719 'Additional Efficiency Improvements - Power demand', M3719 = M2198 = MTInputs F242); read as $M3719 in rows 3691, 3697, 3703, 3709
new_codes.what: One row carries two things: net-exports data (columns D-J) and the power-demand efficiency increment (L:M). The demand formulas read $M3719 as the efficiency term, so the row label misleads.
new_codes.fix: Put the efficiency increment on its own labelled row (or read M2198 directly); leave row 3719 to net exports.
new_codes.effect: None on values (increment 0 by default); a reader of the row label takes the efficiency term for a trade term.

new_codes.title: Fuel-use block: mislabelled parameter and fuel rows
new_codes.where: Mitigation C2199:C2201 ('Tax in nominal or real terms?', 'Exponential option or linear' twice) beside K2199:M2201 (road, residential, industrial additional efficiency, MTInputs F243-F245); E2385 (LPG 'Road'), E2386 (kerosene 'Industry') on all-sector rows (codes shp.lpg.all, shp.ker.all); D5615, D5722, D6072, D6083 'Other oil pinducts'
new_codes.what: Column C of rows 2199-2201 labels the carbon-tax settings of column E, while every fuel row reads K:M of the same rows as the additional-efficiency term; the sector labels of the LPG and kerosene shadow prices do not match their all-sector codes; a typo in four rows.
new_codes.fix: Give the additional-efficiency increments their own labelled rows; label the LPG and kerosene shadow-price rows 'All'; correct the typo.
new_codes.effect: None on values; formula audits misread the additional-efficiency term as a carbon-price setting.
